biological.citation: Mutation-specific excitatory network study - SCN1A-deficient excitatory neuronal networks display mutation-specific phenotypes (PMID: 37467479)
biological.summary: Patient-derived iPSC excitatory neuronal networks on multi-electrode arrays showed phenotypes that depended on the SCN1A mutation type. Loss-of-function mutations were distinguishable from missense mutations, and pore-domain mutations from voltage-sensing-domain mutations. Networks did not segregate by clinical severity. All patient networks were aggravated at febrile temperatures. Anti-seizure drugs affected GEFS+ networks but not Dravet networks.
biological.sample_size: Panel of patient-derived lines, including one family with febrile seizures, GEFS+ and Dravet phenotypes from the same mutation

biological.citation: Antisense oligonucleotides increase Scn1a expression and reduce seizures and SUDEP incidence in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome (PMID: 32848094)
biological.summary: TANGO ASOs that modulate non-productive splicing (poison exon 20N) increased productive Scn1a transcript and Nav1.1 protein in human cell lines and mouse brain. In Scn1a+/- mice, a single ICV dose reduced electrographic seizures and SUDEP.

biological.citation: Antisense oligonucleotides restore excitability, GABA signalling and sodium current density in a Dravet syndrome model (PMID: 37812817)
biological.summary: In Scn1a+/- mice, parvalbumin interneurons had reduced sodium current density, biphasic excitability with depolarization block, and reduced GABAergic signalling to pyramidal neurons. Pyramidal neuron excitability was unchanged. ASO-84, which targets exon 20N splicing, restored interneuron firing, sodium current density and GABAergic signalling. This indicates Nav1.1 acts mainly in PV interneurons.

biological.citation: The gain of function SCN1A disorder spectrum: novel epilepsy phenotypes and therapeutic implications (PMID: 35696452)
biological.summary: Whole-cell voltage-clamp of NaV1.1 variants showed gating changes consistent with gain of function and hyperexcitability. Epilepsy variants gave a mild gain of function. Familial hemiplegic migraine type 3 variants gave a stronger one, with increased persistent current and larger action current amplitude. The variants cluster in inactivation regions, unlike Dravet variants. Sodium channel blockers reduced seizures in 81% of gain-of-function patients.

biological.citation: SCN1A gain of function in early infantile encephalopathy (PMID: 30779207)
biological.summary: T226M Nav1.1 expressed in mammalian cells showed hyperpolarizing shifts in activation and inactivation and enhanced fast inactivation. This is a biophysical gain of function. Dynamic action potential clamp and computational models showed a left-shifted rheobase and greater susceptibility to depolarization block. This is a 'functional dominant negative' effect that explains the severe phenotype.

biological.citation: Biological concepts in human sodium channel epilepsies and their relevance in clinical practice (PMID: 32090326)
biological.summary: SCN1A, SCN2A, SCN3A and SCN8A show significant constraint for both truncating and missense variation. Age at seizure onset relates to temporal SCN gene expression. The functional effects of variants at corresponding channel positions are similar across SCN subtypes, but the clinical outcome differs with the neuron types in which each channel is expressed.

biological.citation: Developmental progression of respiratory dysfunction in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome (PMID: 40924494)
biological.summary: Scn1a+/- mice had a blunted ventilatory response to CO2/H+ before seizures began, and this worsened over time. Some also had blunted hypoxic responses, and respiratory severity correlated with mortality. Pharmacological activation of Nav1.1 rescued activity deficits in retrotrapezoid nucleus neurons, implicating Nav1.1 in inhibitory control of RTN neurons.

biological.citation: Medial septum parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory neurons are impaired in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome (PMID: 40622667)
biological.summary: SCN1A is also expressed in the medial septum. Patch-clamp in Scn1a+/- mice showed dysfunction of medial septum PV inhibitory neurons, with altered firing-pattern subtype proportions. Cholinergic neurons were unaffected, so Nav1.1 loss affects PV neurons selectively.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Long-read sequencing and profiling of RNA-binding proteins reveals the pathogenic mechanism of aberrant splicing of an SCN1A poison exon in individuals with epilepsy
biological.summary: Variants near the SCN1A intron 20 poison exon (20N) increased its inclusion and reduced Nav1.1 protein in patient iPSC-derived neurons. RNA-antisense purification with mass spectrometry in a splicing reporter in HEK293T cells identified differential binding of SRSF1, SRSF3 and HNRNPR to the variant constructs. RNA immunoprecipitation with ddPCR validated these interactions, indicating these RBPs regulate poison exon splicing.
biological.sample_size: 5 variants in 5 individuals; 3 patient iPSC lines

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - SCN1A mutations in a SIDS cohort
biological.summary: SCN1A variants G682V and the cis compound variant L1296M/E1308D were found in 2 of 10 SIDS cases with hippocampal abnormalities. Heterologous expression showed partial loss of function for both, linking SCN1A channel dysfunction to SIDS.
